headline: Disciplined Deliveries and Robust Demand Keep the Nation's Largest Industrial Market Tight
bullets: Overall vacancy stood at 8.3%, up 10 bps QOQ but down 130 bps YOY on robust demand and disciplined deliveries.
Construction held flat at 31,199,625 sf, or 3.0% of stock, with build-to-suit projects at 11.2 msf, or 35.9% of the pipeline, the highest share since 2018.
Asking rents reached a new high of $8.74 net psf, up 10.0% YOY, while landlords held firm on face rents and 3.75% to 4.00% escalations in tighter submarkets.
outlook: Robust leasing activity has eliminated most supply risk, and Cushman & Wakefield projects expected deliveries may increase overall vacancy by only 40-50 bps or less depending on the pace of demand through 2026, with deliveries likely totaling 31.6 msf by year-end.
narrative: ECONOMY Metro-level employment data for January 2026 was delayed by the government shutdown in November. As of Q4 2025, Dallas/Fort Worth (DFW) employment grew slightly at a pace of 0.4% year-over-year (YOY) to reach 4.3 million. Population growth continued at 110,040 new residents over the last 12 months, increasing 1.2% YOY.

Texas manufacturing and service firms indicated slowing growth in March in Dallas Fed surveys, with many noting an increase in uncertainty due to geopolitical events and potential supply chain disruptions. Nevertheless, firms in both sectors continued to expect growth in employment and capital expenditures over the next six months, indicating generally favorable conditions for industrial real estate.

DEMAND Leasing activity totaled 18.5 million square feet (msf), the strongest first quarter on record and the fourth highest quarterly total in Dallas history. In addition, leasing activity in Q4 2025 was revised up to 19.5 msf, the second highest quarterly total on record. As a result, leasing activity re-accelerated to 64.1 msf over the past 12 months.

Demand was robust across all sectors, particularly in third party logistics, e- commerce, manufacturing, and data center-related suppliers, contractors, and servicers. 14 “big box” users over 500,000 sf leased 13.7 msf over the past 12 months, approaching the pace last observed in the post-pandemic boom of 2022 and 2023.
